fetters.c: Hello, I'm Vodyanitsa, the Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe. As you can see... Well, I mean, look at my ears. Pretty unusual, right? That's because I'm a "Water Imp." But that's neither here nor there. All you need to know is that I'm the best singer in the entire Korolevskiy Troupe.
...Hmm? Keep it down, I think I hear someone whispering again... Hehehe, lemme see if I can make out what they're saying...
Well, if there's nothing else going on, I might as well do some rehearsing... Uh, no, forget it. I don't wanna disturb the locals again. Or the animals...
Whew... I've been on dry land for too long — my skin's getting dry. I'm in serious need of some underwater time.
Ah, what a lovely day. Perfect for some underwater relaxation.
Aw, where'd the rain go? What a downer...
A vast expanse of white. Hmph, if nothing else, it's a clean aesthetic.
Ugh, it's so hot and dry... Get me back to the water...
Good morning. I just finished my vocal warm-ups. Did you hear me? Yeah, I'm not surprised. My singing voice really carries.
Alright, time for some lunch. My poor voice is so tired after the morning I've had. I'll go get Odette, then we can grab a quick bite.

Whew, the day is finally over. I'm gonna take a dip in the lake in a bit, you wanna join me? ...Huh? What are you so scared of? Pssh, no, I don't drag people underwater and try to drown them! I'm not THAT kind of Water Imp! But I can do that if you want!
Nighty-night~ You should get to bed — I'll be getting up pretty early tomorrow to do my vocal warm-ups. Of course, if you have any song requests, I'm more than happy to oblige.

fetters.sourceTitle: 关于沃雅妮莎自己·歌声的魅力
fetters.c: Unfortunately, my voice doesn't cast any kind of magic spell on people that drives them crazy. People listen to me purely because I sing well. ...Ooh, although on that note, I actually have a joke about the Domovoy, hehehe... Ahem, never mind, forget I said that. Odette will start glaring at me again if I tell it.

fetters.sourceTitle: 关于沃雅妮莎自己·审视
fetters.c: Whether you're a performer or not, if you truly want to be seen by other people, you have to accept the scrutiny that comes with it. Nothing worth having in this world comes without a price. And if it ever seems like you got something for free... Heh, that just means that fate has secretly decided the price for you.

I turned my fish tail into two legs to make walking on land easier. ...What price did I pay? None! Hmph, for us Water Imps, leaving the water behind is a big enough price to pay already. What else do you wanna take away from me, the right to drink fresh water? I suppose you'd make me subsist entirely on fruit juice or Fonta, wouldn't you?

Still, I can't just stay in Snezhnaya all the time. Sometimes, I'll follow the waterways and swim around the world to hear what singers in other places sound like. I've been to Liyue, Fontaine, Inazuma, Sumeru... Huh? Has anyone ever noticed me? Hehe, of course. That's why there's legends about merfolk, mermaids, sirens, and so on all over the world. Natlan was something else, though... That place is hot. With a capital H, O, T.

Oh, this old thing? Yeah, it's pretty. Makes a nice piece of jewelry, I guess. But as a singer, I don't have much use for it most of the time. And as for "the gaze of the gods"... Hmph, I'm more interested in the gaze of my audience.

The water quality in Fontaine is amazing! Last time I traveled to Fontaine to watch a show, I couldn't resist diving underwater. I stayed there for ages, and gulped down loads of water. But I guess I must have made too much of a splash, because I caught the attention of someone from the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol who was training on the shore. She thought I was drowning... She came rushing to the rescue, yelling at the top of her lungs. But, uh... I just flicked my tail and whoosed away, hehehe. Then watched from a distance while she treaded water and looked around in confusion. It was pretty hilarious. Anyway, I waited until she was safely back on shore before I went underwater again to carry on gulping away. It really is delicious, you know. You should join me next time.

Do you know about Frostfin Whales? They communicate using "whale songs," which most people can't even hear, let alone understand. But we Water Imps have no trouble understanding them, and we can even learn the language. I've actually gotten to know a Frostfin Whale named Hitova — real good-natured. Back when I was traveling all over, I hitched a ride off of her. I'll have to introduce you if I ever get the chance. I'm sure she'd be happy to take us both out for a ride.

Whenever Odette is rehearsing, I listen along intently to her dance steps from backstage. She lands, then jumps, spins in the air, then lands again... Every motion is cleanly executed with impeccable timing. Just by listening, I can tell her dancing is flawless... Hm, why don't I go out front to watch? Hehe, because I wanna hide backstage and jump out at her afterwards! Sure, I haven't managed to scare her yet, but I have to keep trying. Otherwise, all that time I've spent hiding backstage would've been for nothing!

I wish that Mr. Smarty Pants would stop trying to make scientific breakthroughs while he's watching the show. The theater is not a glorified study hall, and it's certainly not a refugee camp for escaped office workers. He'd better start taking our performances seriously... or I'll be forced to... *sigh* What am I saying — there's nothing I can do about it, especially since he technically does abide by theater etiquette... Hmph, next time I see him in the audience, I'll have to perform one of my louder pieces. Let's see how well he can concentrate on his work then.

I've always wondered if Alyosha's puppies can understand my songs. I'm guessing probably not, since we can't understand puppy songs either. Matter of fact, I don't even know if they can sing at all... But my lullabies work like a dream on them. I'll barely make it through the opening verse before they're all out like a light. ...Hmm, not sure what that says about my singing, though... Is that good or bad?

Thanks to Miss Vesna, those theater ticket scalpers know not to push their luck. She said she's planning to invite me to host a small conference on ticket scam prevention soon, and I'm supposed to be singing a song at the end to wrap things up. The thing is, out of all the songs I know, I don't think there's a single one for satirizing scam artists. ...Wait, tactical deception in war should count as a scam, right...? Ummm... maybe I could sing a war epic...?

I'm not personally very familiar with Miss Danica, though of course, her reputation precedes her. She must have had it tough, answering to the Tsaritsa on one hand while having to deal with Miss Vesna on the other... Ahem, but uh, you didn't hear that. At least, not from me.

If Her Majesty the Tsaritsa comes to see a show at the theater, I'll break out the old songs of the Water Imps for her. ...How old? Well... Not so old that only the Tsaritsa has heard them before, but definitely old enough that you can hear the dust coming off when you start singing them. I just hope it doesn't get in people's eyes. Wouldn't want to make everyone cry.

Is Miss Columbina no longer a Harbinger? Huh, shame. I always thought she had a great singing voice. Her songs were like the moonlight itself: so soft and gentle, yet somehow icy cold. So present and vivid, yet so impossibly out of reach... Heh, I only hope she finds somewhere she can belong, with good friends who understand her songs.

Mr. Tartaglia often brings his family to the theater. Harbingers get free admission, although family members have to buy tickets like everyone else. Fortunately, he always manages to secure tickets for his family. Oh, right — you know Tonia, don't you? She's a huge theater fan. She might even join us when she grows up. If that happens, I guess Mr. Tartaglia will have to get used to visiting the theater even more often.

Lady Arlecchino sometimes brings a few children to watch a show at the theater. One of them has these cat ears — Lynette, I think her name was? Yeah, that's right — she and the boy, Lyney, are both excellent magicians. They actually performed a magic show here on the stage one time during an end-of-year performance. The only time Lady Arlecchino tends to come without the children is to watch "The Mountain Sparrow"... I suppose she prefers to enjoy that show alone.

Miss Sandrone always seems to be in a hurry whenever she comes to see a show. Sometimes she grits her teeth, sometimes her eyes twitch... Other times, her face is completely blank, but she's crumpled some scrap paper into a ball. If I didn't know better, I'd say someone was forcing her to come against her will... But far be it from me to speculate who has the power to force her into anything. Still... Heh, she always seems a little more relaxed by the end of the show. So at least she's not completely wasting her time.

The captain? Oh, you mean THE Captain? Well... to be honest, I've never really had a proper conversation with him. I mean, we've exchanged a few brief words on occasion when we've bumped into each other after a show, but that's about it. Still, I can tell that he's a very serious and upstanding sort of person. Even in the audience stalls, he sits there completely straight, like a flagstaff or a pillar. I get the sense that nothing could ever faze him, let alone break him, not even the fiercest storm.

fetters.sourceTitle: 想要了解沃雅妮莎·其一
fetters.c: So, you got some burning questions, huh? Well, ask away — but for every question you ask me, I get to ask you one, too. It's only fair. Don't worry, I won't ask any difficult questions. Just, uh... Y'know, the things I haven't found the answers to anywhere else.

fetters.sourceTitle: 想要了解沃雅妮莎·其二
fetters.c: Sorry to burst your bubble, but we Snezhnayan Water Imps aren't some mythical creatures who drive sailors mad with our alluring songs, or pay some enormous price to walk on land, only to turn into sea foam if we break our vows. Nope, we're just ordinary people living ordinary lives, like everyone else in Snezhnaya.

fetters.sourceTitle: 想要了解沃雅妮莎·其三
fetters.c: Since that incident, almost all the Water Imps have left Snezhnograd. My dear brothers and sisters invited me to leave with them, but I turned them down. I'm sure the citizens of Snezhnaya would be saddened if the day ever came that they could no longer hear our songs. And if Snezhnaya forgot our songs, the other Water Imps and I would be sad, too. That's why I stayed behind to keep singing. To prevent sadness all around.

fetters.sourceTitle: 想要了解沃雅妮莎·其四
fetters.c: ...Times have changed. Snezhnaya is a completely different place today. Inevitably, it's changed the way I relate to my singing, too. As time goes by, it's like the songs become... heavier, more layered and complex than ever, and I can't help but feel... Anyway, I don't like being like that, so I made a simple rule for myself: Whenever I feel like just going home, I find ten people in Snezhnaya and see if they like my singing. If even one out of ten genuinely likes my songs, I will stay. But if not even one person in ten cares, I'll return to my brothers and sisters.

fetters.sourceTitle: 想要了解沃雅妮莎·其五
fetters.c: Heh, I don't know whether to call it good or bad luck, but every time I've sought out ten people to get their verdict, I've always found at least one who is genuinely willing to listen to my singing. Some were just starting out, others were deep in the trenches of the most heroic struggle of their lives, and some were calmly preparing for the final leg of their life's journey... Even if that were the entire audience, I and any of my kin who linger still in the theater would continue to sing for them. So, what about you? Do you enjoy my singing? Hehe. Be careful how you answer — we Water Imps have exceptionally good hearing. I'll know whether you're lying from your heartbeat alone. Ready? I'll count you in: Three, two...

Whenever I'm in a good mood — or a really bad mood — I dive into the water, close my eyes, and let the current carry me around. As I drift along, I listen to all the sounds carried on the waves: Little fishies gathering together, their scales brushing against one another... giant whales singing deep, drawn-out songs as they call out to their partners far away... bubbles rising up from the deep, then bursting... Occasionally, when I drift by a city, I'll even hear the fishermen chanting as they cast their nets, children laughing as they leap into the water, and ships creaking as they prepare for a long voyage or return to port... Listening to the sounds of the world like this is truly magical. Do you want to try it? If so, I'll take you with me next time.

I don't like sounds laden with too much meaning. Singing is just another sound, like the news carried by the waves, the crisp sound of falling leaves, or the pitter-patter of running footsteps... The greater a sound's burden, the harder it is to understand, and the more unpleasant it is to my ear.
Mm... Anything sweet, really. Although, preferably nice and cold, with just a dash of syrup, and... Huh, now that I say it out loud, I guess I'm just describing ice cream.
If there's no moisture in it whatsoever, I just cannot handle it. I mean, I can physically force myself to swallow it, sure, but my throat will feel like it's being torn to shreds on the way down.

Ooh, this is delicious! I guess you remembered what I told you about my favorite foods, huh? You have a pretty good memory. Next time, it's my turn to make some food tailored to your tastes. ...Yeah, I know you've never explicitly told me before, but don't worry — I already know. I have my ways of finding these things out.

Thanks. Oh, by the way, do you still remember my favorite food? I told you last time. You do? Hmm... Guess you've got a pretty good memory. I'll have to give you something tougher to remember next time, hehehe.
...Maybe next time, I should be clear about my food preferences in advance. Or maybe I can teach you how to make something really delicious.

Happy Birthday! I've set aside your gift. You can open it later. It's just some small trinkets, toys, and whatnot... Eh, but that's not the important part. You're free now, aren't you? In that case, come with me! We're going to my echo chamber. I got someone to buy me a Dance-Off Stage from Natlan a few days ago, along with a whole bunch of weird and wonderful instruments. I'm working on the best music event Snezhnaya's ever seen, and guess who's the first person to receive an invitation? That's right, it's you! Come on, let's sing the night away!
Ahem, ahem... Alright. Sounding good.
I think I just reached a new high note.
Ah, my voice is feeling stronger than ever.
Whoo! Time to sing the whole night through!
Listen closely.
Start with a warm up.
Taking the stage.
This is more like it...
Heehee, look at my fish tail!
Woo! Hahahaha!
An elegy to mortality.
An ode to eras past.
Everyone, lift your voices!
Wow! Look at all these shiny treasures! Quick, grab 'em!
This looks alright, I guess. Could be fun to play around with.
Is that it? Huh. So much for "treasure" chest...
Hehe... Heh...
I'm done playing.
...Oh, you'll regret that.
Hey! What are you doing!?
Get over here! Stop messing around!
You're all here...
Waves... carry me home...
A high note... to end on...
I slipped...
Hmph! I'm not done yet...!
Face me in the water if you're so tough!
I'm not built for dry land...!
My ears are burning.
Here I am. What's up?
*clear throat* Mm, my vocal cords are all warmed up.

stories.c:
A long, long time ago in Snezhnaya, Water Imps dwelled all over the city. Some sang glorious melodies on the stage, while others cheerfully hummed lighthearted tunes through the streets and alleyways. Then there were the others who preferred to slip into the water, where they would lure curious passersby to the water's edge with their haunting, dreamlike songs, only to then suddenly leap up and splash the unsuspecting onlookers full in the face before vanishing, giggling, back beneath the surface with a flick of their tails, leaving their victims floundering between anger and laughter...
But, as time passed, the stages and alleyways of Snezhnaya quietly lost their singers, and the melodies beneath the waters, carried by unseen currents, began flowing soundlessly toward a distant silence. People began to whisper uneasily among themselves, wondering if those haunting songs from the deep might drift away from them forever...
Then, one morning, people learned that Vodyanitsa was still performing on the stage of Korolevskiy Theater, as though the days of old had never faded and the joy of bygone times had remained just as it always had been.
Hardly anyone knew why she stayed — nor did anyone dare ask her to her face, unless they were prepared to never secure another interview with Miss Vodyanitsa ever again.
Maybe, she had stayed on in order not to disappoint the audiences who so adored her singing? Or maybe she was just unwilling to exit that dazzling stage? Or perhaps... there were other reasons significant enough to make her swim against the current, even if it meant bidding farewell to her own kind...
But for Vodyanitsa's audience, delving into the answer to that question is utterly meaningless. The only thing that matters is that they can continue to listen to the captivating voice of the Water Imp.
Of course, if you want to be swept away by her song...
"Standing tickets? Uh, sorry, but we don't sell those here at the theater at the moment... And no, we don't allow our patrons to bring their own chairs either."
"Crack the doors open a little? The draft would leave everyone inside freezing..."
"My apologies, but the theater isn't hiring any day cleaners at the moment!"
...First, you need to get a ticket.

Once, Vodyanitsa sang with a joy as bright and untroubled as the childhood her kin had shared in Dalegrad.
In those days, the Water Imps knew no bounds. They wandered wherever their hearts desired, giving freely their songs of blessing to every living thing.
...Then Vodyanoy Donbettyr, the Lackland, entered into league with King Miscislav the Blood-Devourer. The swift and fearless children of the waters became the strength behind Miscislav's ascent, winning him glory and, in time, a crown. Yet Donbettyr's daughter, Vaselisa Vodyanovna, could not bear the sight of her kin's cold blood frozen across the lake. With blood-pink flowers of ice cupped in her hands, she stood upon the water's edge and mourned each silent soul.
At last, she departed. All among her kin who would no longer bear arms followed in her wake, and together they made their way to the court of Emperor Monomakh Snezhnyi.
There, the Emperor conferred a title upon her. Vaselisa Vodyanovna accepted it, for she knew that if she wished to receive the favor of the Pale Star, she must first bear the name bestowed upon her.
Yet when crown, treasure, and lands were offered to her in turn, Vodyanovna refused them all. The exiled Water Imp said only to the Tsar:
"I have no need of this crown, for it can rest only upon a brow weighed down by a heart just as still."
"I have no need of this treasure, for it can satisfy only those who chase after empty gain."
"I have no need of these lands, for waters and earth were never meant to belong to any one sovereign."
"I ask for nothing else. I wish only that the children of the waters cease whetting their blades to songs of sorrow. Let them sing for every soul that carries true love within, and let every song they raise belong to their own hearts alone."
Emperor Monomakh assented to Vaselisa Vodyanovna's petition, and from that day onward, no Water Imp beneath the Pale Star would ever again be made to serve the desire of another heart. The Emperor and Vodyanovna bound themselves by oath as well: Even should a Water Imp freely offer to go to war, none would be required to bear steel. And so the covenant was kept. Weaponless, the Water Imps walked among armies without ever joining in the slaughter. Yet neither did they forget the protection Monomakh had granted them.
They became couriers of tidings, bearing military dispatches from camp to camp and the whispered letters of lovers from heart to distant heart — the latter being, by all accounts, their favorite charge. They carried the wounded swiftly downriver, guiding and drawing their rafts with such mastery that it seemed little short of miraculous. And when terror prowled the camps beneath the cover of night, their songs lulled anxious soldiers into peaceful sleep. Many of those tunes outlived the war and passed into the musical canon.
In time, there came a day when no blood darkened the waters of the lake, and the Pale Star cast its radiance unto the furthest reaches of the land. The long lament beneath the snows reached its final verse, and upon the frozen banks of Dalegrad, the blood-pink flowers of ice never rose again.
Then Vaselisa Vodyanovna gathered the Water Imps before her and spoke to them plainly:
"Go. Sing as freely as the waters run, for every precious thing beneath the sky, and for every sincere heart that holds this world dear."
"Tell the snows of spring and the blossoms of winter, the autumn sun and the fruits of summer, that never again need anyone lose their way in the passing of the seasons."
"Tell the waters and the earth that all creation may now hear the hymns that should have been sung to it long ago."
"Tell farmer and craftsman, soldier and sovereign, and every soul in between: The world is worthy of love, and worthy of praise."
And so, at last, Snezhnograd rang with the unfettered songs of the Water Imps.

As accomplished singers even among the Water Imps, Vodyanitsa's parents soon rose to renown throughout Snezhnograd. Theaters across the city competed for the honor of hosting them, and the pair seldom turned down an invitation.
But the stage they loved best was the one at their own small estate, where they would gather a chosen few for intimate performances. There, worldly distinctions seemed to fall away, and the only ticket worth having was a heart that loved song.
Vodyanitsa was only a child in those days, but even then, she knew how a song ought to be heard. Whenever the fae and townsfolk below began to sing together, she would quietly open her window and watch from above in the dim gold of morning. Her parents would lead, and all around them rose voices of every kind, meeting and parting, weaving apart only to embrace again within the same melody. As their song climbed into the morning air, anyone listening could almost believe that no difference had ever divided them at all.
They were all born of the same world, and in that alone, none stood apart from another.
Little Vodyanitsa blinked, remembering something her parents had once told her — the same words once spoken by Vaselisa Vodyanovna, the "Zmey Maiden" herself.
"Go. Sing as freely as the waters run, for every precious thing beneath the sky, and for every sincere heart that holds this world dear."
Vodyanitsa thought, "Oh my, there are so many people in the world! They must all have so many things they truly love. There are so few of us Water Imps, so how are we ever supposed to sing for everyone?"
"You needn't think that far ahead, dear Vodyanitsa," her mother said gently. "The trick to singing is to think only of how to sing the next song well."
"That's right. One song, then another, then another after that," her father chimed in with a smile. "Swimming is much the same. You swish your tail once, then once more, and little by little, you find yourself somewhere far away."
"Then I'm going to be singing for ages and ages," Vodyanitsa said.
"You are," her mother and father replied. "We Water Imps will be singing for this world for a good long while yet."
"But that's all right. We have all the time we need to love it."

Vodyanitsa's songs had always been sweet and lilting, much like the countless little "performances" she had given all across Snezhnaya.
Of course, only a small number of them had ever taken place beneath the lights of some grand, gilded stage.
She had found far more amusing places to perform beyond the theater walls. Admittedly, her choice of venue could give the occasional passerby quite a fright. At these impromptu "concerts," she was never merely the singer — she listened, cheered, waited for her turn, and clapped along for everyone else.
Vodyanitsa once followed a peddler making his way along the riverbank, calling out his wares as he went. He hummed a little tune with no name, toys chiming softly in his hands while children laughed and chased one another at his heels. The melody was bright and easy, and though the children stumbled through it, they joined in all the same. Years passed, and when the peddler finally went to his long sleep, those children returned to the old riverbank as grown men and women. They laid flowers upon the water in his memory, and just then, a fin shimmered briefly beneath the surface. A moment later, from somewhere along the river came the faint strains of the song they had known as children. They began to sing before they even realized it. Their voices followed the current together with the Water Imp, and as the melody drifted downstream, they wished with all their hearts that it might find its way into the dreams of their old friend.
Vodyanitsa once paid a visit to a half-built railway station, where she became fascinated by the work chants of the men repairing the trains. The workers could not imagine why a little Water Imp would willingly sit in such a place, much less do so without earmuffs. But she seemed perfectly safe, and not even the sparks could scorch the hem of her dress, so they shrugged and returned to their work. Hammers rose and fell. Steel rang against steel. Flame hissed against ice. Then, when the weather turned and a blizzard came sweeping in, everyone finally laid down their tools. Someone brought out the liquor, and cups were raised to chase the cold from their chests. That was when Vodyanitsa, who had listened in silence all day, suddenly began to sing. Her humming followed the cadence of their own shouted calls. For a heartbeat, the workers simply stared, and no one quite knew what to make of it. Then they roared with laughter and answered her. Soon, her bright voice and their coarse, thunderous chorus were ringing together through the steelworks and the storm.
And so Vodyanitsa continued her wandering, following heart and current alike. She found herself among freshly sown fields, where farmers sang simple verses to keep track of the seasons, among schoolchildren who chirped and giggled and composed mocking little songs for their friends on the spot, and outside brand-new restaurants, where shy owners, red-faced but determined, tried to lure in customers with tunes they had only just invented...
Soon enough, everyone knew of the little Water Imp who had no great patience for proper stages. Given the choice, Vodyanitsa would always rather be outside the city, singing to the open wilds.
Like a stream carving its own channel through the land, Vodyanitsa made a path simply by moving forward. And wherever her wandering current flowed, all things in its wake seemed to answer her with laughter.

Then the Pale Star's lingering radiance went out, and with it faded the songs that had once filled every street and alley of Snezhnograd.
The Water Imp who used to haunt the entrance of a restaurant, pestering the owner for lunch and promising to pay in song, no longer came. Before he left, he handed over every page of music he had written, suggesting that perhaps they might be counted toward the meals he still owed. The Water Imp who liked to sit on the roof with her legs dangling over the eaves, deliberately singing dreadful little songs, was gone too, though not without leaving behind the favorite flower she always wore in her hair for the little Domovoy who had spent so many days jumping up and down beneath her, shouting at her to stop disturbing the peace. The Water Imp who forever complained that Snezhnograd did not have a single proper place for a bath was gone as well, having already made plans with a Vila to seek out the finest frozen lake in the north, if only so she could prove whether a Water Imp had any reason at all to fear the cold. So too was the Water Imp who criticized every jewel in town and argued endlessly with one particular shopkeeper. Before leaving, he gave her the finest pearls and gemstones he possessed and, at last, told her what he had never quite managed to say before — that he had always trusted her to make the most beautiful jewelry in all of Snezhnaya. And then there was the Water Imp who had spent day after day trying to coax flowers from the frozen soil. She was gone too. She had finally found seeds that might work, and after all that searching, the difficult part was already done. All she needed now was time for the first buds to push through the soil in her pot.
The people had long suspected that the Water Imps would not remain forever, but knowing that did little to soften the day when silence finally settled over the city and not a single song remained. Nothing in daily life truly ceased because of it. Doors still opened, meals were still served, and work still carried on. Yet somewhere among all those ordinary things, a tiny vacancy had crept into the world, almost too small to name and far too persistent to ignore. Everything was still where it had always been, but somehow the whole of it no longer felt quite whole.
It was like returning to a familiar home and finding one treasured picture missing from the wall, or seeing a beautiful hat stripped of the trim that had once given it character. It was like a feast in which every dish was perfect save one, made strangely dull by the lack of a little seasoning. Such omissions might mean very little to a stranger, but to those who had known and loved these things for so long, their absence announced itself at once.
Still troubled by the sense that something was missing, people opened their windows and leaned into the silence, listening for even the smallest trace of sound...
Then, to everyone's surprise, a faint thread of song rose out of that silence. No one had expected to hear a thing, and yet there it was, drifting from the great Korolevskiy Theater. Curious, people began making their way toward its entrance almost without thinking. By the time they gathered there, a Water Imp had stepped before the crowd and proclaimed in a clear, ringing voice:
"Today's performance at the Korolevskiy Theater will go on as scheduled!"
A man in a hat was the first to find his voice.
"You... stayed?"
"I did." The Water Imp smiled as though there were nothing remarkable about it. "My performance isn't finished yet. It's meant to run for seven days, and we've only reached the second."
"And when the seven days are over... will you leave then?"
A girl with exhaustion written plainly beneath her eyes asked.
Vodyanitsa looked out over the crowd. Every face turned toward her, toward the last Water Imp in the city who still stood upon a stage and sang.
"No," she said, smiling. "I have far more songs in me than seven days could ever hold."
"Now then! Tickets ready, everyone, and inside you go! There's warm sweet wine by the aisles."
"And we've laid out blankets, hand warmers, and opera glasses as well. Take whatever you need."
"Come on, no dawdling — the show is about to begin!"

"...Dear Vodyanitsa, we miss you. Just as we told you before, if ever you wish to return, you will always have a home with us."
So ended another letter from a faraway lake untouched by winter's ice. The Water Imps who had returned there sent their messages with the river fish, asking after their little sister and calling her home. They knew that Vodyanitsa, like most of their kind, was unlikely to thrive in the city as it had become. Too many hearts there burned hot and restless, and too many voices clamored to be heard. Everyone seemed determined to claim the stage for themselves, while almost no one had the patience to share it, much less join another in harmony. Before long, the result ceased to resemble music at all. Voices crowded against one another, each struggling to rise above the next, until what should have been graceful and harmonious dissolved into little more than a harsh tangle of noise. Whatever else the city might still be, it was no longer a place made for singing. And where singing could no longer flourish, listening had grown difficult too.
Vodyanitsa lingered over her thoughts for a long while before beginning her reply.
"I do want to come home. But just as I told you before..."
"...Whenever I start thinking of returning, I first find ten people in Snezhnograd and listen to see whether they truly care for my songs."
"And if even one of them is listening with all their heart..."
Of course, there were people in the city who adored Vodyanitsa's singing... Why wouldn't they? A ticket to hear the Korolevskiy Troupe's Prima Donna was a prize in itself — scarce enough to make a splendid gift, and impressive enough to win almost anyone's favor. Better still, if one could say they had spoken with the prima herself, the story would travel nicely through any salon. With a flourish added here and there, even the most jaded members of high society might be persuaded to look impressed. Her handwritten letters were rarer still, the sort of thing no amount of money could easily buy. Though, naturally, that only made them more valuable to those who wished to collect such things, and a determined collector might offer an even better price. Then there were the rumors that the prima occasionally sang to herself by the roadside or out in the wilds. With the proper timing, one could always contrive to be passing by at precisely the right moment.
...Would I choose to stay for people like these?
But people like these had never truly wanted to listen to my songs. What they wanted was to turn those songs into whatever pleased them most, burdening my voice with one hollow crown after another. They did not see, and had no wish to see, how each crown pressed a little harder against my throat, weighing down songs that should have been bright and effortless until they grew heavy and strained. And somewhere along the way, as they covered my voice beneath all those things they wanted it to mean, they buried their own sincerity just as surely... They no longer wish to love me as I am.
And yet Vodyanitsa's pen never touched the paper. She did not write what she was thinking, nor did she ask her kin to come and carry her back to the quiet homeland she had left behind.
Because there had still been a time when their affection was real. The person who now passed rare tickets around to curry favor had once been thrilled beyond measure to receive one himself. He had dressed in his best, settled into his seat, and watched so intently that he scarcely seemed to blink. The one who now liked to boast of knowing Prima Vodyanitsa had once, as a child, gone with his friends to pick wildflowers. Together they had woven them into a garland and left it by the back door of the theater, and when Vodyanitsa appeared, the children cried, "You sang so well!" before running off together before she could catch them. And the girl who had since grown into a skilled singer really had met Vodyanitsa by chance beside the river. In those days, her voice was still clumsy and unsure, and she stumbled badly whenever she tried to sing. Before long, the two of them made a habit of practicing there together. Whenever Vodyanitsa talked on and on about music, the girl would listen with eyes that shone like dew beneath the sun.
The true feeling they had once carried had simply changed with the current. In some, it became ambition, forever searching for a higher shore to climb. In others, it became the restless hunger to gather and possess. In still others, it swelled slowly into vanity...
But Vodyanitsa remembered what had come before all of that. Her songs remembered too. They remembered that once, these people had loved her voice with all sincerity, and that in loving it, they had also loved the people they themselves had once been.
And somewhere within that endless current of time, perhaps one sincere moment is enough for love to have been real.
At last, the solitary Water Imp completed her reply.
"...So I am willing to stay for them, too."

stories.sourceTitle: 有关尾巴的保养细则（节选）
stories.t: A Few Rules for Keeping Your Tail in Good Condition (Excerpt)
stories.c:
...Above all else, remember to soak your tail in fresh, clean water on time. Do not add milk. Do not add flower petals. Do not add fruit. And please, for the love of all things watery, stop adding anything that looks remotely like seasoning! This is tail care, not a fish-tail stew!
One more note: The finest water for tail maintenance comes from the Court of Fontaine. Goodness, if I could bathe in Fontaine's waters every day, my tail would probably be in such perfect condition I'd never stop admiring it. If the opportunity ever comes up, I'm taking a nice long holiday and disappearing underwater in Fontaine for a while.

"...Vodyanitsa, the house is full. We sold every last ticket."
After a quick glance beyond the curtain, the announcer let out a breath of relief. At least one fear could finally be put to rest: The theater would not lose its crowds simply because the Water Imps had left. Yet the relief hardly had time to settle before another concern began to gnaw at him. Vodyanitsa was no stranger to the stage, and her singing had always been more than respectable, but... now? With expectations running this high, "more than respectable" might not be enough to carry the evening.
"Good," Vodyanitsa replied with a smile. "We'll go ahead as planned. I'm counting on you for the opening announcement."
The announcer nodded, though the motion did little to calm his nerves. He hesitated for a moment before finally asking:
"What are you planning to sing...? Ah, but... no, that's not really the point, is it? It's just... heavens. All the other Water Imps are gone. You're the only one left to sing now."
He could not quite bring himself to say the rest aloud, though the problem was obvious enough. Normally, there was a system. Each Water Imp sang what suited them best, and while one stood beneath the lights, the others rested. It spared their voices while keeping the program varied, and even when someone took the stage alone, every song was chosen and placed with care so that there was always just enough time for the throat to recover.
But tonight... Tonight, one look at the excited audience beyond the curtain told him that none of that careful pacing would matter. Good heavens, he knew that much already. The moment Vodyanitsa tried to leave the stage, they would applaud her back onto it. Then they would do it again. And again... In the space of a breath, he imagined countless ways he might step in and save her from being worn down, only for each one to fall apart before it was even fully formed. The audience beyond the curtain was like a vast plain starved of rain. No matter how fierce the current that swept across it, they would not let it pass without taking every last drop.
"Oh, I haven't decided. I'll sing one song, see where it takes me, and go from there."
The little Water Imp said it with a grin and watched as disbelief slowly gave way to horror on his face. Then she calmly slipped a throat lozenge into her mouth.
"Y—You haven't—? No. No, no, dear, that won't do at all. You need a plan. Please tell me you have a plan."
"Look at the people out there. Really look at them. Do you honestly think they came here prepared to be satisfied by something as neat and sensible as a plan?"
Vodyanitsa stood before the curtain and peered through the narrow slit between its folds. Beyond it, the hall thundered with voices, and through that small opening spilled a familiar warmth and tumult she had not felt in a long while. Excitement filled the air, certainly, but beneath it she could feel impatience as well. Doubt. Melancholy. Grief. The whole hall seemed to lean toward the stage, every eye resting on the curtain, tense with the certainty that it would not remain closed for long.
What could possibly satisfy them? What could soothe a heart gone dry from silence?
"Song," Vodyanitsa thought. "Of course it's song. What else could they have come here wanting? What else could they be hoping for? What else could all that expectation be asking of the stage?"
"Song. Endless song. Boundless song. Every song that was, every song that is, and every song that will one day be sung."
The announcer stared at her, dumbfounded. A moment later, his years in the theater began to pick apart the meaning behind her words.
"Hold on. How long, exactly, are you planning to sing alone? Even with a Water Imp's voice, there has to be a limit..."
Vodyanitsa merely shrugged, letting his concern slide past her. Then she brightened at a sudden thought. "Actually, if I'm the only Water Imp in the theater now, doesn't that technically make me the prima?"
"W—Well, no, not technically... There's usually an official selection, but..."
"Perfect. We'll call tonight the selection."
The announcer barely had time to blink before Vodyanitsa pulled back the curtain and strode straight into the spotlight. The audience jolted at her sudden appearance, and for a moment, the entire theater seemed to hold its breath. Then the applause came crashing down from the seats like a cataract.
"Welcome, everyone, to the Korolevskiy Theater! Tonight, there is no setlist. No program. I'll sing whatever comes to me, and I'll be the only one singing."
As she spoke, the theater's would-be Prima Donna raised both hands.
Every eye in the theater followed the movement, drawn to Vodyanitsa and the water-blue Vision that had suddenly appeared in her grasp.
"Well," Vodyanitsa thought, "that should make keeping my voice in shape a little easier."
"Maybe there is a chance I can keep singing until no one out there has the strength left to applaud."

costumes.name: Surging Resonance
costumes.description:
Vodyanitsa's outfit. It is said to draw inspiration from various cultural traditions related to the Water Imps. For more details on these cultural elements, please direct them to Miss Vodyanitsa.
Of course, do wait until she is taking a break from her performances if you wish to ensure that she has time to spare.

skills.d:
<color=#FFD780FF>Normal Attack</color>
Performs up to 6 consecutive strikes.

<color=#FFD780FF>Charged Attack</color>
Consumes a certain amount of Stamina to trample opponents in front of her.

<color=#FFD780FF>Plunging Attack</color>
Plunges from mid-air to strike the ground below, damaging opponents along her path and dealing AoE DMG upon impact.

Calls forth Spirit Blades passed down through generations of the Vila to deal <color=#80FFD7FF>AoE Anemo DMG</color>, then switches to the <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430001}Armed for Action{/LINK}</color> mode and gains 2 stacks of <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430002}Sword Essence{/LINK}</color>.

<color=#FFD780FF>Armed for Action</color>
DMG dealt by Vesna with her Normal Attacks, Charged Attacks, and Plunging Attacks become <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo DMG</color> that cannot be overridden by another elemental infusion instead. She will also summon a wind pinion that attacks the opponent at the same time, dealing additional <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo DMG</color>. Each time the wind pinion is summoned, Vesna will regenerate a certain amount of <color=#FFD780FF>Sword Essence</color>.
Vesna can consume <color=#FFD780FF>Sword Essence</color> to unleash the special Elemental Skill <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430003}Windborne Sword{/LINK}</color>, which deals to the opponent <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo DMG</color>.
Each use of the special Elemental Skill <color=#FFD780FF>Windborne Sword</color> in the same instance of <color=#FFD780FF>Armed for Action</color> will increase the level of <color=#FFD780FF>Windborne Sword</color>, beginning from Lv. 1 to Lv. 3 max, for more <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo DMG</color>. Using <color=#FFD780FF>Windborne Sword</color> at Lv. 2 and Lv. 3 will also summon <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430004}Spirit Blades{/LINK}</color> which deal <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo DMG</color>.
Vesna will exit the mode when its duration ends or when she has used <color=#FFD780FF>Windborne Sword</color> at the highest level 3 times. Exiting will clear all remaining <color=#FFD780FF>Sword Essence</color> she has accrued.
Additionally, when in this mode, Vesna's resistance to interruption is increased.
<color=#FFD780FF>Radiance: Stellar Swirl</color>: DMG dealt with the <color=#FFD780FF>Spirit Blades</color> becomes <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo DMG</color> that is also considered Stellar Swirl reaction DMG.

Summons multiple <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430004}Spirit Blades{/LINK}</color>, dealing <color=#80FFD7FF>AoE Anemo DMG</color>. Also gains a stack of <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430002}Sword Essence{/LINK}</color>.

After Vesna uses the special Elemental Skill <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430003}Windborne Sword{/LINK}</color> or the Elemental Burst <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#S11435}For the Tsaritsa!{/LINK}</color>, she also gains 1 stack of <color=#FFD780FF>Disciplinary Action</color> which lasts 20s. Max 6 stacks, and the duration of each stack is independent of the others'.
When she has <color=#FFD780FF>Disciplinary Action</color> stacks active, the <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430004}Spirit Blades{/LINK}</color> summoned by Vesna will deal DMG equal to (100% + 10% × Disciplinary Action stack count) of the original DMG instead. All active stacks of <color=#FFD780FF>Disciplinary Action</color> are cleared when Vesna uses the Elemental Skill <color=#FFD780FF>The Art of Victory</color> or when she leaves the field.

<color=#FFD780FF>Radiance: Stellar Swirl</color>: Vesna will gain the corresponding effect based on the Elemental Type of her party members: 
· For every <color=#99FFFFFF>Cryo</color> or <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo</color> character in her current party, Vesna's ATK increases by 6%; and
· For every character of all other Elemental Types in her current party, Vesna's Elemental Mastery increases by 25 instead.

When party members trigger Cryo Swirl, it will be changed to a Stellar Swirl reaction, and party members' Base DMG for the Stellar Swirl will be increased based on Vesna's ATK. Every 100 ATK she has increases the Base Stellar Swirl DMG by 0.7%. The maximum DMG increase that can be gained this way is 14%.
After a party member triggers a Stellar Swirl reaction nearby, Vesna enters the <color=#FFD780FF>Radiance: Stellar Swirl</color> state for 8s.

Holding on Sprint or Jump when Vesna is not in combat will cause her to enter the <color=#FFD780FF>Coursing</color> state.

<color=#FFD780FF>Coursing</color>
Continuously consumes Stamina to hover in mid-air. Sprinting or tapping Jump to go higher expends additional Stamina. Including the hold on Jump that triggers <color=#FFD780FF>Coursing</color>, Vesna can go higher up to 3 times in each instance of the <color=#FFD780FF>Coursing</color> state.

Additionally, in Snezhnaya (excluding Nod-Krai), when Vesna is switched onto the field while the currently active party member is in mid-air and not in combat, she will immediately enter the <color=#FFD780FF>Coursing</color> state and regenerate 50 Stamina. This effect can trigger once every 10s, and does not take effect in Domains, Trounce Domains, or the Spiral Abyss.

talents.d:
When in the <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430001}Armed for Action{/LINK}</color> mode, Vesna can unleash <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430003}Windborne Sword{/LINK}</color> at the highest level 4 times instead of 3. Also, each time she enters the <color=#FFD780FF>Armed for Action</color> mode, she will not consume <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430002}Sword Essence{/LINK}</color> the first time she uses <color=#FFD780FF>Windborne Sword</color> at the highest level.
Additionally, Vesna deals 20% increased Stellar Swirl reaction DMG when in the <color=#FFD780FF>Armed for Action</color> mode.

The Ascension Talent <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#P1432101}Rite of Spring's Procession{/LINK}</color> is enhanced: Vesna gains the maximum number of <color=#FFD780FF>Disciplinary Action</color> stacks when she enters <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430001}Armed for Action{/LINK}</color> mode. Vesna's ATK is increased by 40% when she has maximum <color=#FFD780FF>Disciplinary Action</color> stacks.
You must unlock the Ascension Talent "Rite of Spring's Procession" to gain access to the above effects.

Increases the Level of the Elemental Skill <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#S11432}The Art of Victory{/LINK}</color> by 3.
Maximum upgrade level is 15.
The Ascension Talent <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#P1432201}Truth Prevails{/LINK}</color> is enhanced: Its ATK and Elemental Mastery bonuses increase to 3 times their original values.

Increases the Level of the Elemental Burst <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#S11435}For the Tsaritsa!{/LINK}</color> by 3.
Maximum upgrade level is 15.

Tapping on Normal Attack or Elemental Skill in the 5s after Vesna uses <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430003}Windborne Sword{/LINK}</color> at its highest level will unleash the secret Vila ability <color=#FFD780FF>Windborne Sword: Transpose</color>, dealing <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo DMG</color> at 150% of Vesna's ATK as well as summoning <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430004}Spirit Blades{/LINK}</color> which deal an additional instance of <color=#80FFD7FF>Anemo DMG</color> at 200% of Vesna's ATK. If Vesna is in the <color=#FFD780FF>{LINK#N11430001}Armed for Action{/LINK}</color> mode, she will also summon a wind pinion to perform Coordinated Attacks against opponents.
Additionally, Vesna's Stellar Swirl reaction DMG dealt is {LINK#N11190007}<color=#FFD780FF>elevated</color>{/LINK} by 20%.

fetters.c: Hello, dear friend. Commander Vesna of the Druzhna. The pleasure is all mine. The gun salute and honor guard are in position and ready for your grand welcome. Of course, if you're not one for fanfare, I've also arranged a more private welcome ceremony. Come on, this way~
The Druzhna takes orders only from the Tsaritsa, so they cannot be at your beck and call. But Vesna the Vila is happy to be of service, my dear friend.
Isn't this outfit just gorgeous? It was a personal gift from Her Majesty. Hehe, that's right, feast your eyes.
What paperwork? Oh, I finished it ages ago — flew through it. Now it's time to get out on patrol. C'mon, let's go~
Fae can absolutely catch colds. When they get wet, it's important to flap them dry right away. T—The wings, I mean.
In the snow, the slightest imperfection in your camouflage can be fatal. So tread carefully, dear friend.
I know what you're thinking — and I agree. My wings look their most dazzling in the sun.
Ah... Hehe, very nice. The Vila just love a good breeze.
Just wondering... When are we heading back to Snezhnaya again?
A new day! Good morning, Snezhnograd!
Off we go to Podvorye Restaurant, come on! My treat, of course. As always!
The Korolevskiy Troupe is debuting a new show tonight. Featuring Prima Donna Vodyanitsa's high soprano, Miss Odette latest choreography... and a few "new friends."
Pssst... You can't be asleep already. Come out for a late-night walk? The aurora is great tonight!

fetters.sourceTitle: 关于薇斯纳自己·「魔法武器」
fetters.c: See these little things flying around me? They're my magic weapons, my own creations. Each one is a blend of elemental energy and my own will, so they've inherited something of my personality as well. Which is to say, it's possible that they might pester you to play with them. Don't mind them... Though of course, if you have time, please indulge them, hehe!

fetters.sourceTitle: 关于薇斯纳自己·司令官
fetters.c: Who says a commander needs to be strict and imposing? Pshh, that's for people with no presence. I don't need it~ I think we're quite similar in that regard.

I get it, I get it. There are all sorts of rumors flying around about me, and you want to know the truth. Well, that's fine, we have plenty of time for that. But in return, I want to know the truth about you, too, down to the very last detail.

I don't like the idea of "accompanying" someone on a journey. It sounds romantic at first, but when you think about it, the word "accompany" makes one person the protagonist and the other a mere sidekick.
The truth is, every step we take is our own, as are the things we experience and the ways we grow along the way. So, I won't say that I'm "accompanying" you on your journey — rather that I'm glad to have the pleasure of your company on what happens to be, for now, a shared journey. Think of it like this... you're walking along, minding your own business, then at some point you turn your head and notice: Oh wow! Haha, look at that — seems like we're both going the same way!

Stellar Linchpins are beautifully designed. Absolutely a collector's item. Actually, Moon Wheels aren't bad, either. Always wanted to get my hands on one. As for Visions, though... Not interested at the moment, sorry.

Oh, you mean this old thing? Beautiful, isn't it? It's a family heirloom, you know. Much, much older than I am. A true antique, in fact, worthy of a museum. Sometimes I use it as a magic wand, sometimes as a pointer when giving a class, and sometimes as a commander's baton... Ah, just look at me, giving it the chance to relive its glory days at this ripe old age, rather than locking it up in a bank vault somewhere to gather dust. My ancestors would be lining up to sing my praises if they knew!

The Frostfairy Flower is a thing of beauty and resilience, surviving in spite of the brutally cold environment. It also has a very distinctive pattern. I like gazing at it through half-closed eyes as I shake my head, hehe — it creates a dreamy effect, like looking through a kaleidoscope. That said, I'd advise doing that in a private place with no one else around.

I've apprehended far too many self-righteous fools who wish to oppose Her Majesty. Their grand speeches about conquest? All show and no substance. They have neither the strategy to launch a rebellion nor the competence to see it through. Compared to those would-be revolutionaries... No, I take that back. They don't even deserve to be mentioned in the same breath as Her Majesty.
My point is, serving the Tsaritsa is not only my duty as a Vila. It's also my personal choice as Vesna.

Her Majesty always speaks the word "compassion" with an icy sting to it. She says it's a curse imposed upon the gods by the Heavenly Principles, not genuine love. But I very much disagree. Whenever I return from a campaign against monsters, Her Majesty adds "rest well" at the end of her personal decree. And after the Ruler of Life's power was reclaimed, she sensed how disappointed I was, despite my efforts to hide it, and sent the unclaimed portion back to me...
Someone in her position has no obligation to do any of these things. At the risk of sounding presumptuous, I've always believed that the question of whether a god is truly loving can only be answered by their people. So why shouldn't my verdict count?

Oh, dearest Miss Danica... Don't be fooled by her serious and brooding demeanor. We got up to all kinds of mischief together when we were little... Like the time we plotted to steal Teacher's mask right off of his face. We made it all the way up onto his shoulders before getting caught! Sure, we didn't quite pull it off, and yes, we got punished — had to stand at attention on a frozen lake for hours... Ah, but anyway, that's besides the point! She was the one who came up with that crazy idea in the first place! She was every bit the troublemaker I was. And now she gives me that look all the time, like she's the adult and I'm the child. I mean, puh-lease. I'm actually the older one.

We have good intel that certain suspects are using bizarre events like "Quarreling Contests" as a front to conduct illegal business transactions, the rowdy crowd serving as a handy distraction... And so, it falls to me to intervene.
To that end, I've taken the liberty of signing Danica up. She's a master of deadpan takedowns and hitting people where it hurts. No one can out-quarrel her, so she'll definitely buy me tons of time.
Counting on you, Danica!

I always remember how he looked from behind. So sturdy and reliable, like a steadfast mountain. I never imagined there'd come a day when that mountain would fall. Or at least... I didn't think it would come so soon. He always used to say, "In a real war, you don't get the chance to say goodbye." Of all the ways to prove it to me... Surely, he could have given me one last chance before the end, but he didn't...
I'll never let that go, Teach.

Some people skip through the world with a pep in their step, most of them full of hope for what tomorrow will bring. Not him. His steps are always slow and heavy. I always felt that he and my teacher were similar people. I guess it's because they both hide unimaginable sorrow beneath a mask, bearing all the pain of the past on their shoulders.
Mr. Mayor speaks with such eloquence and composure at the Snezhnograd Veche, and he makes it look so effortless. He can really command the room.

Now, I'm not saying that a Druzhna Commander's salary is low, but it can get a little tight if you're an avid collector who also enjoys treating people to meals... No, oh, no no no, I didn't mean it like that! I wasn't finished. Ever since I can remember, my family's spare funds have been managed by the Northland Bank, and thanks to Mr. Pantalone, the compound returns have grown our wealth quite substantially. Basically, I don't have to worry about money at all. So next time we're out, it's still my treat, and no need to hold back!

Sandrone fully embodies what it means to be a lady. Her words may be highly aggressive in nature, but her impeccable logic makes it impossible to find fault with her... Hehe, it really fascinates me. I must learn how she does it.
Mitya often joins me for hijinks. He's forever sneaking out of the Armory, and the three of us always have a blast! Why "three," you ask? Because there's me, Mitya, and his ever-so-clever scarf.

Every one of Miss Vodyanitsa's songs is simply beautiful. I love hearing them live. At times they fill me with joy, at other times they move me to tears, just like everyone else in the audience. Sometimes, everyone stays behind after the show ends and suddenly breaks into song together. Well, funnily enough, I just so happen to have a conductor's baton in my hand. And even more funnily, I've noticed on several occasions that Miss Vodyanitsa quietly blends into the crowd after changing out of her stage outfit, puts on a hat, and sings a harmony for the group.

I have to be honest — every time I see Miss Odette at a court gathering, I find myself stealing a glance at her constantly. After all, as well as being a member of the Fatui, she has a special alter ego that makes her hard to ignore... Hmm? Why, her role as prima ballerina of the Korolevskiy Troupe, of course. What did you think I meant?

I get it, I really do. I mean, how could any little puppy resist the urge to chase a pretty butterfly through the "howling" winds? Hmm... Maybe I'll steal Danica's breakfast and feed it to Tugarin, then ask Alyosha to put in a good word for me, so he doesn't come charging at me the moment he sees me...
Hehe, so how would you like to get to know me? Surely, we're not just going to chat? Well, that's no fun... Hmm... Can't we play a game of "Truth or Dare" instead?

We Druzhna are the Tsaritsa's personal guard, answering directly to Her Majesty. Our duties aren't just limited to neutralizing monster threats and going into battle — they extend beyond military affairs. In all matters concerning Her Majesty's authority and honor, we are bound to answer her call unconditionally and remove all obstacles from her path.
However, Her Majesty is inevitably spread a little thin while the grand endeavor against the Heavenly Principles is ongoing. So until the dust has settled, I am more than happy to assist her with the fun stuff— Ahem, I mean, the more trivial matters, such as ribbon-cutting ceremonies and attending banquets on her behalf.

I have an eclectic collection of treasures. Jewelry, ancient books, oil paintings... Anything that makes me happy is worth adding to the collection. And I have to have it the moment I lay eyes upon it, not a single second can be wasted! You know the saying, don't you? "A spoon is dear when lunch time is near." If you wait until after the initial thrill has passed before acquiring it, it loses it appeal. So, if I want it now, I must have it now.

After Tsar Monomakh's sacrifice, Snezhnaya went through a period of great turmoil. My forebears stood firmly by the Tsaritsa's side. So, as I stand here on their shoulders today, do I really possess the strength to do justice to their legacy? Hehe, I've put words to the question in your mind, haven't I? Well, now it's your turn to voice the answer that's in mine. Go ahead~

On the eve of the battle against the Ruler of Death, I extracted "Seals of Life" from many people. Everyone's definition of a beautiful memory varies. Some cherish sitting around the fireplace with family, chatting idly. Some fondly remember sitting alone by a train window, watching the aurora drift silently across the night sky. Still others are satisfied simply pulling a sled out for some ice fishing...
Those memories are like iridescent bubbles, filled with an effervescence and vitality that just makes you want to exclaim: "Ah, it's so good to be alive!"
Yet, those so-called heavenly beings can crush those bubbles with ease, without giving a single word of explanation. What gives them that right?
From that moment on, for me, the fight against the Heavenly Principles was no longer solely about assisting Her Majesty.

When I was very young, my family arranged for me to take painting, dance, and singing classes. As I got a little older, I took up fencing, horse riding, and the like, hehe... More recently, I've been getting into opera, theater, and collecting my little treasures... In short, the word "bored" doesn't exist in my dictionary.

Don't listen to Danica's nonsense — there is absolutely nothing wrong with my driving skills. It's called being one with the vehicle! Just wait till my driving ban is lifted. I'll take you for a spin!

When it's so cold out, there's nothing cozier than gathering everyone together for some nice hot stew! Tell you what — I'll host, and you and Paimon can bring along some cooking ingredients. Anything you like will do~
Hehe! I'm slipping all those annoying veggies onto Danica's plate! Ugh... but they always come right back to me...
Oh, don't mind if I do! I'm going to savor every last bite.
Mmm... Quite a feat of culinary ingenuity... I think I'll take another bite.
Oof... I'm sorry, I already ate! But let me box them up for Danica~

Ding-dong! The moment has arrived! You have no idea how hard it was for me to hold it in yesterday... But I had to, because saying it early is bad luck — you might get swallowed up by a snowstorm! Now, I can finally say it: Happy Birthday, my dear friend. May you stand as strong as the birch tree, never defeated by the wind and snow.
Alright, that part's done. Next, tradition dictates that I've got to give our birthday superstar a few gentle tugs on the ear...
First lesson in boot camp: Only those who do not stand firm and do not yield to the wind and snow are qualified to stand guard by Her Majesty's side.
Second lesson in boot camp: Your sword arm must never tremble.
Third lesson in boot camp: We do not weep before our foes.
You, dear friend, have taught me a lesson from beyond boot camp: To reserve a soft touch with which to embrace those I defend with my sword after the blizzard has died down.
Form up!
Salute.
Raise your swords!
Coming through~
More where that came from.
Kindest regards.
Haha, alright. Let's play!
Locked on — no escape!
For the Tsaritsa!
Hoho, another piece for my grand collection!
One for you, one for me, one for Her Majesty, and another for me! None for Danica, hehe!
Well, lookee here!
A commander stays on the field.
Don't worry, I'll dodge the rest...
Ahem... Just a temporary setback...
Fall back. The Druzhna will take it from here.
Don't push yourself, my dear friend.
My wings... are clipped...
Long live... the Tsaritsa...
I'm not in pain... just denial...
Excuse me?
Huh?
Very bold!
How rude!
Time for a patrol~
I hope you have something fun planned!
At your service, commander...

stories.c:
In Snezhnaya, the clan name "Strivozha" is one of certain importance.
This ancient Vila bloodline, which was already in existence long before Snezhnaya's turbulent early days, has weathered countless storms and earned countless honors over the years.
Vesna is evidently worthy of the name. Radiant and graceful, she exudes effortless refinement and quiet poise... well, at least most of the time.
A veritable free spirit, she refuses to be bound by the norms of polite society. This can often lead to surprising antics.
Sometimes, she drives the train at such reckless speeds that all it leaves behind is a blur — and a reprimand waiting for her at the end of the line. At other moments, she carefully, meticulously, scrupulously slips a chosen slice of sour lemon onto a colleague's plate...
But no one would ever question Vesna's virtue or honor, for they come from her sword rather than superficial mores and gestures.
The Druzhna is the blade wielded by the Tsaritsa herself, and Vesna is its keenest edge.

It was early February when winter had yet to release its hold. On the outskirts of Snezhnaya stood a secluded country estate of House Strivozha, wrapped in silence.
Grand Duchess Benigna had spent the nine months of her pregnancy in peaceful retreat here. Hers was an easy, untroubled existence, filled with little more than long hours among the flowers and greenery she tended herself.
Few gardens could boast such strange and uncommon flora. Among its collections were rare varieties sought out across the land: summer buttercups, white currants, five-petaled lilacs, berryless elderberries...
Then there were the curiosities created by House Strivozha's own perfumers and apothecaries: hybrids of dill and coriander, of saffron crocus and Snezhnayan winter aconite...
Some ancient strains were said to have survived since the days of Saint Strivozha. One of these survivors now held the Grand Duchess's attention: a red fern the color of flame.
It had stood in the garden since before she became its keeper, and never once in all those years had it strayed from the old rhythm of the seasons.
Autumn saw it fade, and through winter it lay dormant. Not until spring returned would its tender crimson fiddleheads emerge, tightly curled like the head of a violin, heralding another season of life.
But that year, winter had not yet relinquished its presence, and already the fern's stems were swelling, lush and full with a vigor wholly foreign to the season.
At its base, a fine blush-red fuzz was spreading over the soil, threaded with tiny, translucent scales shaped like hearts.
Within them, sap could be seen coursing slowly through delicate veins, like the first pulse of blood from a newborn heart. This was the earliest form of the fern's new fronds.
The Vila had always possessed an instinctive affinity with nature, and Grand Duchess Benigna knew at once that what she was seeing was no ordinary growth. For the fern's natural cycle had been brought forward by a full month.
She got to her feet and went to examine the other parts of the garden, only to find out that wherever she went, the surrounding plants immediately began to show the same signs of premature growth.
She was about to inform her father and husband when, perhaps from the strain of pregnancy — or perhaps because of some long-pending fate written high above — she stepped on a patch of unmelted ice.
With a startled cry, she fell.
The fall cost the garden its rare crimson fern. It also brought Benigna's child to follow the example of all those early-blooming shoots — emerging into the world a full month before she was due.
Thankfully, the little one was unexpectedly healthy, and her mother made a full recovery within just a few weeks.
And yet, it was the winter itself that came to an early end that year. Birches budded ahead of their season and grass pierced the frozen earth, bringing the long cold to an untimely close.
The story eventually reached Her Majesty the Tsaritsa, who came to the Vila estate in person to visit the Grand Duchess and her extraordinary newborn daughter.
It is said that the Tsaritsa took such a liking to the child, so much so that she gave her a name herself.
Vesna — the spring that walks beside her.

When Vesna was little, her mother would lull her to sleep each night with warm little stories.
Those stories were all made up from the flowers and herbs in her garden, and most began in much the same way:
"Vesna, my brave little snowball flower..."
"Vesna, my lucky little lilac..."
"Vesna, my clever little cornflower..."
Night after night, nestled in the tenderness of her mother's words, Vesna felt perfectly safe and warm.
Of all those one-of-a-kind endearments, there was one Vesna remembered more clearly than any other:
"Vesna, my immortal little flame fern..."
She knew that fern well. There was nothing else like it anywhere in the world, and nowhere else could it be found but in the gardens of House Strivozha.
It was a fern cultivated by the hand of her ancestor, Vaselisa von Strivozha, The Pure One, Lady of the Vila of Veneter.
Thousands of years ago, she presented Emperor Monomakh with a perfume blended from the fern's fronds, earning a renown that would endure for generations.
The fern came to embody the purity, benevolence, sincerity, and immortality of Saint Strivozha and the Vila.
But the legendary fern had been crushed in the accident that brought Vesna into the world, and from that day onward, it never grew again.
The once immortal life had left the garden, just as the immortal Saint Strivozha herself had long since departed from her faithful descendants.
Young Vesna thought she had discovered a truth: nothing in this world was truly everlasting. Sooner or later, everything had to leave.
And so she looked up at her mother, eyes shining with conviction, and declared,
"Mom, I understand what you were trying to say. Nothing lasts forever. Even spring has to leave someday."
"So when spring is here, we should enjoy spring. And when summer comes, we should be happy to see summer. Autumn and winter too."
"We just have to make sure we don't waste any of our days. That's what you mean, right?"
Benigna stared at Vesna in surprise, but a smile soon tugged at the corners of her lips.
"My clever girl. You've thought this through even better than I have. And yes, of course you're right."
"But think a little harder. Surely there must be something in this world that lasts forever..."
Vesna's eyes went wide. "What is it? What is it?"
Benigna pulled her into her arms, bent down, and planted a soft kiss on her tender cheek.
"Oh, silly girl. My love for you will last forever."

In the eyes of the Vila elders, Vesna had all the makings of a legend from the very beginning, born as she was with the blessings of spring and winter upon her.
Yet even with every expectation that she was destined for greatness, the pace of her growth never ceased to amaze them.
At one year old, while other Vila her age were still crawling about and babbling, Vesna could already name every flower and herb in the garden.
At two, when the first chitinous tips of her peers' scaled wings were only just beginning to show, she was already riding the wind on her own wings, circling the estate a dozen times over without coming down.
And by three, just as other young Vila were beginning to learn the art of blending flowers and herbs into fragrances and elixirs, Vesna's own creations had already become fixtures upon the dressing tables of ladies at court.
Within that tiny frame coursed a vitality far beyond the ordinary, as though the spring that had arrived alongside her all those years ago had never truly departed, but instead lived on in every radiant smile that crossed the girl's face.
Of all the elders who delighted in Vesna's smiles, only one truly understood what kind of power the girl might be displaying.
That person was Pyotr, Grand Duchess Benigna's father, Vesna's grandfather, the reigning Grand Duke of the Vila.
On the night of Vesna's fifth birthday, after the celebrations had drawn to a close, Grand Duke Pyotr summoned his young granddaughter to his study and entrusted her with a secret of immense importance.
It was a history older even than the Silver Court of Veneter, one that reached back to the very origins of the Vila, to the age of Hyperborea.
It is said that, in that distant age, the Angel of Angels stole a fragment of power from one who must not be named. Passed from hand to hand through the ages, that fragment eventually vanished into the bloodline of the Vila.
The strange signs that accompanied Vesna's birth — spring itself arriving ahead of its time — and the astonishing speed of her growth all pointed to the same conclusion: that ancient power had awakened within her.
Its name was Life.
At the time, Vesna was still too young to understand the full weight of that word. Even so, what her grandfather told her next still struck deep.
"Everyone knows we Vila stand for sincerity, honor, benevolence, and above all, our unwavering loyalty to Her Majesty the Tsaritsa."
"And yet, from the time of Grand Duchess Glowatza five hundred years ago to this very day... not once have we Vila truly had Her Majesty's trust."
Had those words come from anyone but her own grandfather, Vesna would never have believed them.
But before she could ask why, he placed upon her young shoulders a burden no child her age should ever have been asked to bear.
"Vesna, pride of our people. You are the only one in our family for five hundred years fortunate enough to awaken the power carried in our blood."
"And in those same five hundred years, you alone have been blessed with a name bestowed by Her Majesty herself."
"Perhaps the fate of House Strivozha for the next five centuries now rests in your hands."

After the age of five, Vesna was never seen at a public school again. Her grandfather instead brought masters from various disciplines to the estate, each of them charged with overseeing a part of her education.
Her days were soon filled from morning to night with lessons meant for the very best. There was no longer time to run off and play with her friends, nor were there many chances to roam freely through the garden at home.
Even outings into the countryside with her mother were strictly rationed by her grandfather. All of it was justified because Vesna was the hope of House Strivozha.
Little by little, her time ceased to be her own. And as it dwindled, so too did the bright, springlike smile that had once seemed forever upon her face.
Vesna could never quite decide whether the Tsaritsa's distrust of the Vila truly existed, or whether it was merely something her aging grandfather had convinced himself of.
Another five years passed in much the same way, until one stormy winter night, when the arrival of a very special tutor changed everything.
According to her grandfather, securing this particular teacher had taken no small amount of effort. He had pulled every string he could and spared no expense to persuade them to come.
That night, Vesna sat stiffly in the study, waiting with a knot of unease in her stomach. Before long, the door eased open, and a diminutive visitor quietly stepped inside.
The visitor shrugged off a snow-dusted coat, revealing the face that had been hidden beneath the shadow of the hood. The moment Vesna recognized it, a small gasp escaped her.
Her mysterious new tutor was none other than Pulcinella, The Rooster, Mayor of Snezhnograd, Presiding Member of the Snezhnograd Veche, and the Fifth of the Fatui Harbingers.
The Snezhnaya's highest-ranking chief executive glanced around the room, then went to fetch a chair from the corner himself, one nearly as tall as he was. He set it before Vesna, took his seat, and spoke in a kindly voice.
"Good evening, my dear Miss Fern. I hope you'll forgive me for speaking with your mother beforehand. She suggested that little name might help put you at ease. I hope it did the trick?"
The mention of her mother and that familiar old nickname certainly helped lower the tension on Vesna's shoulders. "Yes, Mayor Pulcinella. I feel much better now."
The Rooster smiled and gave an approving nod, "I'm glad. You're very fortunate to have a mother like yours. Your grandfather, though... Grand Duke Pyotr can be rather less comforting company, can't he?"
A little of Vesna's unease returned. She could not tell what the Mayor meant by the question, and certainly did not dare answer it carelessly.
Fortunately, The Rooster raised a hand, sparing her the need to answer, "Your grandfather must have told you that he went to considerable trouble to secure me as your teacher. What do you make of that?"
This question seemed harmless enough. Vesna thought for a moment before answering, "If Grandfather really had the power to arrange such a thing, then you would have come long ago, Mayor Pulcinella."
The Rooster smiled broadly and gave his mustache a thoughtful twirl, "It seems I really should have come sooner to meet such a clever young lady. And you are quite right. The truth is, I am here at Her Majesty's behest."
Without waiting for Vesna to respond, his expression grew a shade more serious, "Her Majesty sent me to put one of your doubts to rest. The crisis your grandfather, Grand Duke Pyotr, fears is no figment of his imagination."
"To Her Majesty, House Strivozha has never been entirely beyond suspicion. Of all the seats on the Snezhnograd Veche, only a scant few are reserved for your family, even fewer than those allotted to the merchant class."
Even with the truth laid so plainly before her, Vesna still found herself unwilling to accept it. "But our family has such a long and glorious history... Why?"
The Rooster cast a mild glance toward the window. "Then I imagine your mother has already told you the story of the crimson fern..."
"The Vila have always had a gift for turning plants into fragrances and elixirs... But did you know that, if fragrance and medicine had a younger brother, his name would be poison?"
"Saint Strivozha may have used the fern for nothing more sinister than perfume, but five hundred years ago, Glowatza of House Strivozha brewed its fronds into mead and used it to poison the former Grand Duke Photius with her own hands."
"She openly threw in her lot with the rebels who had risen against the Tsaritsa. First, she drove an envoy from the Zapolyarny Palace out of her lands. Then, without waiting for Her Majesty's sanction, she began raising retainers of her own..."
"As such, though wary and distrustful of one another, the rebels of the various fae clans were always willing to entrust their secrets to the Vila, leaving her to devise their plans."
"In the end, she handed every last scrap of that intelligence over to Her Majesty, helping her crush the rebellion in one fell swoop. She even surrendered her lands and abdicated of her own accord, all with her honor seemingly spotless. But indulge me for a moment, Vesna, had Her Majesty failed to swiftly defeat those rebellious Volkodlak lords, whom do you suppose House Strivozha's retainers would have turned their swords upon?"
